acks.note: Research's part is done: I diagnosed why the thumbnail doesn't get clicks (its words say million but the title says billion, about 10 small things in it, no sense of scale, a calm face, green on green) and wrote the rules for every future long video as an adopted proposal for the improver. Redoing this video's thumbnail is Studio's lane, and Studio runs next on 18 Nov, after the Saturday upload, so see the notification for how to get it done in time.

Scripts and narration are the improver's lane. I added your note as evidence to the open proposal shorts-voice-back-to-october-pace, which asks for more words and a faster voice: our 1K-view Shorts spoke 200-240 words a minute, and the recent ones only 146-172.

Animation is the improver's lane. I added your note as evidence to the high-priority proposal actions-that-change-things, which caps glow, shake, grow and tag at 25% of actions in favour of things that move and transform; it also covers the bigger framing you asked for.

Demand now comes from breakouts. The daily market scan fetches each channel's subscribers and lists the videos whose views are 3x+ their channel's audience (market.json 'breakout'). Research starts from that list. The topic ranking gives a breakout reference up to +1.0 and a giant channel's ordinary video -0.6, and check-plan fails a reference with fewer views than its channel has subscribers.

Research's part is topics: I added three world-famous pop-culture stories in the shape of our best Shorts (Taylor Swift, MrBeast), one famous thing and one huge true figure. GTA V made $1B in 3 days, and its sequel launches 19 Nov, so it now tops the feed as a trend. Microsoft paid $2.5B for Minecraft. Squid Game cost $21.4M and Netflix valued it at $891M. Hooks and scripts are the improver's lane.

I checked every open feed topic against the one-country brand list. The Costco topic was already used, and no open topic is about a brand only one country knows. Tonight's new topics (GTA, Minecraft, Squid Game) are known everywhere.

Added two curiosity topics of the kind you named: every billionaire's $20.1T shared out to all 8.2 billion people (about $2,450 each, like our 794-view split Short) and Musk's $839B as $100 bills (8,390 tonnes, 'what a billion looks like'). I'll keep at least one such topic in the feed each week.
